osaka_oishii_sake_nakayoshi_nipponbashi.notes: [Izakaya · a quiet sake-and-fish izakaya by Kintetsu Nippombashi] A calm 17-seat izakaya a minute from Kintetsu Nippombashi, run by two people, with fish the owner buys at the market and a deep drink list: over 40 sakes kept in a dedicated fridge, 80-plus shochu and 15-plus umeshu. Start with the sashimi platter, then the rolled omelet, brought out on a hot teppan with extra dashi poured on so it bubbles at the table. Diners also praise the fried hatahata, homemade zaru tofu, whitebait with grated daikon and ponzu, mackerel pressed sushi and monkfish liver with nara-zuke. Dishes can take a while, and one diner found many sakes out of stock. Closed Mondays.

The food is more than snacks: taro dumplings with beef and burdock in a nameko sauce, spring cabbage and prosciutto croquettes, Kagoshima chicken sashimi, fatty bluefin and seared mackerel, and in spring a run of firefly-squid dishes ending in clay-pot rice. PayPay or cash only.

osaka_naniwa_soba_namba_dining_maison.notes: [Soba · soba-shabu and meat dipping soba on Takashimaya's restaurant floor, Namba] The Takashimaya branch of Naniwa Soba, a small Osaka soba chain (four shops) on the seventh-floor restaurant level, with colorful seats. The signature, trademarked, is soba-shabu: Wagyu swished through the house dashi and eaten with fresh soba, as a course from ¥5,000. For a simpler meal, one repeat visitor always picks the meat dipping soba (¥1,300), pork in a lightly spicy chili-oil dip that becomes a rich soup when you add soba water at the end. Also chilled sudachi soba, ume-and-yam soba and an oyakodon set; diners praise the delicate Kansai-style broth. Open to 21:30 or 22:00, later than many department-store restaurants.

The ¥20,000 omakase runs like a small kaiseki: appetizer, three sashimi, grilled fish and chawanmushi before ten nigiri from squid and striped jack to chutoro, sea urchin and eel; there's also a ¥12,000 sushi course and lunch courses that diners call good value. Past highlights include tuna cooked in a salt crust, well-judged kohada and bonito with salt. You can ask for less rice. Closed Mondays.

osaka_tempura_etsu_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Tempura · a 7-seat tempura course counter, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A quiet seven-seat tempura counter a few minutes from Shinsaibashi, where each piece is fried and handed over in front of you. The ¥12,100 dinner course opens with seasonal sashimi (steamed abalone with liver sauce, snow-crab sashimi), then light, crisp tempura, the shrimp especially juicy, with a fresh salad mid-way and a tempura rice bowl or tempura in tea broth to finish. In winter the showpiece is a female crab packed back into its shell and fried whole. Diners praise the warm, joking hospitality and a list of rare sake and wine. A summer lunch set ran ¥1,650–1,980 in 2026. Book ahead; closed Sundays.

osaka_mahoroba_teppan_shinsaibashi.notes: [Teppanyaki · a relaxed teppan counter for Wagyu, lobster and abalone, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, grown-up teppanyaki restaurant in Higashi-Shinsaibashi with a six-seat counter and two private rooms, more relaxed than one diner expected. Black Wagyu is seared to your chosen doneness and cut, and one diner recommends wasabi; a fuller course adds Ise lobster and abalone, at about ¥24,000. Lunch runs about ¥3,000–4,000, and à la carte is possible when seats are free. Good for anniversaries: one diner got a surprise cake. Open daily, lunch and dinner.

osaka_link_coffee_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Coffee · a quiet house-roasting kissa off the Shinsaibashi bustle, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, dim coffee shop just off the busy Higashi-Shinsaibashi streets, part Showa kissa and part mid-century American, with jazz playing and a counter for solo visits. It roasts its own beans and brews each cup to order: ask the owner for a recommendation (one diner was steered to a freshly roasted Mandheling), or try the mocha with its grapefruit-like acidity or the strong blend. The baked cheesecake is the standard partner, smooth and well balanced; coffee jelly is on the menu too. Not everyone was won over: one diner found the coffee ordinary, the dish-washing loud and the stay limited to 60 minutes. Cash only.

The ¥5,500 course is the way in: appetizers, crisp bacalhau croquettes, Tanba chicken piri-piri, a seafood cataplana, then rice or risotto to finish and a freshly baked pastel de nata. Two diners single out the octopus and the port wine, and you can pick a bottle downstairs and pay corkage. Staff are good at pairing wines. One diner missed Vinho Verde. It fills up, so book. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

osaka_banco_cafe_bar_nishishinsaibashi.notes: [Café · an espresso café-bar from noon to 2 am, Amerikamura] A casual espresso bar on the north edge of Amerikamura, by the Hariju building, open from noon until 2 am and as much a day-drinking spot as a café. Order a double espresso, strong and well-roasted, or a cappuccino doppio, at prices one diner called cheap for a city café (¥363–583 in 2024). The homemade tiramisu, light and not too sweet, is the reason two diners came back; paninis and doria cover meals. Tables are well spaced and the style is laid-back: you're left alone. Smoking is allowed inside, there's no restroom, and one diner found the room getting cluttered. Terrace seats.

Courses move from small appetizers to seafood (live abalone grilled in front of you, Ise lobster, scallops), four seasonal vegetables, and black Wagyu with a choice of sauces and salts, then garlic rice or a rich black beef curry. Lunch courses are the value play; one long-time diner noted lunch prices have risen and the 80 g steak now feels small. Chefs are happy to chat. Closed Tuesdays.

anecdotes.text: "The fresh abalone was quickly grilled while still alive, served with its liver and an oriental sauce… We had sirloin cap and strip loin, served with garlic soy sauce, grated ponzu, and several types of rock salt." — June 2026, lunch course.
"It's unfortunate that due to rising costs, the price of the lunch special has increased… The 80g steak portion feels a bit small…" — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員の公式情報): 鉄板焼 神戸 ホテルモントレ グラスミア大阪、大阪市浪速区湊町1-2-3 ホテルモントレ グラスミア大阪 22F、JR難波駅から徒歩1分、地下鉄なんば駅直結、水〜月・祝11:30〜14:30 (料理L.O. 13:30)、17:30〜22:00 (料理L.O. 20:00)、火曜休み、コース料金は税・サ込、バラ科のアレルギーには対応できない、カード・電子マネー・QR可、禁煙、カウンター6席×2、2か月ごとに米沢牛などの特別コース。口コミ(2026年6〜10月): 22階の大きな窓から京セラドーム、神戸、六甲、明石海峡大橋まで、ランチコース、A5の牛のステーキランチ、夜は Maya や Rokko のコース、活けあわびの肝ソース、伊勢海老、ホタテと海老、季節の野菜4種、黒毛和牛のサーロインキャップ・リブロース・ヒレ、ソース2種と塩3種、ガーリックライスか黒カレー (+500円)、赤みそのみそ汁、デザート、ランチは値上がりしてステーキ80gが少なく感じるという声、シェフとの会話。
